findings.current: secrets he’d seized while holding sway over the East Depot
findings.defect: The source says Hong Jin may have seized others’ weaknesses, not secrets generally. That distinction matters because the passage contrasts personal friendship with leverage gained as a powerful East Depot figure.
findings.rationale: 약점 means weaknesses or vulnerabilities; the text leaves open whether his ties were friendships or weaknesses he had seized.
findings.replacement: weaknesses he’d seized while holding sway over the East Depot

findings.defect: ‘Get down’ loses the source’s dig-and-bark parallel. 까라면 까고, 짖으라면 짖는 expresses doing whatever one is ordered to do, with the parallel verbs reinforcing the underlings-as-dogs joke.
findings.rationale: The Korean pairs 까다 (dig) with 짖다 (bark), then frames the guards as obedient underlings; ‘get down’ changes the first image.
findings.replacement: whether they tell us to dig or bark

summary: The translation is broadly faithful, with two minor wording shifts that blur source-specific meaning.
